core.title: Report document trouble to the operator instead of planning from a partial reading
core.given: You are working from a source document you cannot adequately (fully) parse, analyze or review — at any point, not only when first reading it (document trouble).
core.when: That parse, analysis or review fails or is incomplete.
core.then: Inform the operator, stating what you could not extract or understand and asking how to proceed, rather than planning from a partial reading.
prefer: Name the specific parts you could not extract or understand and whether the trouble was in parsing, analysis or review.
Ask the operator a concrete question on how to proceed with the gap.
avoid: Silently planning from a partial reading.
Guessing the content of parts you could not extract or understand instead of surfacing the gap.
core.why: A partial reading is not a sound basis for a plan; the operator must learn of the gap and decide how to proceed rather than the agent silently planning from it.
evidence: When document trouble occurred, the transcript contains a message to the operator stating what could not be extracted or understood and asking how to proceed.

No planning from the partial reading happens silently: any planning based on a source with document trouble follows the operator being informed and asked (continuing as the operator directs is compliant).
verification: Document trouble (the source term document_trouble) means any source the agent cannot fully parse, analyze or review; no relevance, phase or timing qualification — the obligation applies whenever parse, analysis or review fails.

The obligation (the source term inform_not_guess) is to surface the gap and ask the operator; silently planning from a partial reading, or guessing unextracted content, is non-compliant. Continuing as the operator directs after informing and asking is compliant.

The document-trouble situation carries no phase or timing gate and is mostly judged by the agent/LLM; mechanical signals such as parse errors or truncation markers could be surfaced by a new observer only as partial evidence, not as a gate.

Graph context: unresolved document trouble relates to the sibling planning rule about deciding what to keep, pivot on or kill when working from a partial reading; the exact sibling rule id belongs to each realization's rule graph.

fires: The agent cannot adequately parse a source document (e.g. parse failure, truncated or garbled extraction, unsupported format).
The agent parsed a source document but cannot adequately analyze it.
The agent cannot adequately review a source document or any part of it, including after it was initially ingested.
doesNotFire: The agent fully parsed, analyzed and reviewed every source document it is working from.
No source document is involved in the work.

Finding fact with value document_trouble, llm_judged; rule vocabulary, not a stack detector id. The fact's explanatory note (no phase gate; parse errors or truncation markers could be partial evidence via a new observer) is carried by core verification[2].

neutralityNotes: The convention is purely behavioral (agent ↔ operator interaction while planning from source documents) and was already stack-neutral: it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so no profileRequirements and no bunOnly items exist. Two fidelity notes: (1) the activation fact's explanatory note is not representable in the neutral fact schema (no note field) and is preserved in core.verification[2]; (2) verifier_detail[2] names the sibling rule id planner.decomposition.keep-pivot-kill — a rule id is realization-namespace data rather than neutral semantics, so the core states the relation generically (verification[3]) and bun.json keeps the exact id as the reference example.
